$comment: R1260 T5.3 - retest exercise data for Machine B, aligned to MACHINE-B-REPLACEMENT-BUILD-ACCEPTANCE-MATRIX.md (amended twice on 2026-08-11). Authored on Machine A 2026-08-11. DATA AND DOCUMENT ONLY: this file is not a transfer authorization and names no candidate, because no candidate is declared. Delivery to B is owned by R1237 D3, not by this file.

candidate.why: require-clean-tree and check-payload-current both refuse while multiple lanes hold both trees dirty. Every staged binary is either pre-rename or carries no declaration. See DO-NOT-DECLARE-THESE-README.md.
candidate.rule: Every null above must be filled from the frozen copy before this pack is executed. If any field is still null, B must refuse intake rather than proceed - an absent field is not a pass.

registryGuidCarveOut.note: The PASS guid is the UUIDv5 of the OLD appId and is pinned deliberately so the installer replaces a pre-rename install instead of forking beside it. Key names are UNBRACED.

outcomes.failGuidOnly: FAIL - pin lost, install base forked again
outcomes.both: FAIL - the side-by-side defect this row exists for
outcomes.neither: INCONCLUSIVE, NOT A PASS - resolve whether nothing is installed or the wrong key was probed before recording any verdict

priorFindings.name: silent relaunch
priorFindings.symptom: First run from installer completion opened a window. Every tested normal relaunch after a clean close produced no window and exited code 0 with zero-byte stdout/stderr, no Windows Error Reporting entry and no crash report. Executable, Start Menu shortcut, shortcut target plus working directory, and direct launch all failed.
priorFindings.machineAStatusClaim: UNVERIFIED FOR ANY CURRENT BUILD. No A-side lane has demonstrated a clean close-and-relaunch cycle on a declared candidate. Related but NOT the same thing: a lane reports settings now survive a forced port change 4601->4602.

priorFindings.name: publisher identity absent/inconsistent
priorFindings.symptom: Windows Apps & features and the uninstall registry entry showed no publisher.
priorFindings.machineAStatusClaim: PARTIALLY EVIDENCED. A lane measured the built executable's VersionInfo CompanyName as 'ToolsEnabled, Inc. in formation'. That is the FILE resource, which is a different field from the Installed Apps publisher, which comes from the uninstall registry Publisher value. B's finding was about the registry field. Do not let a correct CompanyName be quoted as clearing this row.

priorFindings.name: uninstall retention and non-obvious completion
priorFindings.symptom: Uninstall removed the registry entry, the 78-file install directory and the Start Menu shortcut, but presented no clear progress window and retained ALL 59 user-data files totalling 9368864 bytes, including shell-state.json with saved Tan-theme state.
priorFindings.machineAStatusClaim: OPEN, AND THERE IS A DESIGN CONTRADICTION TO RESOLVE - see contradictions[0]. Separately a lane reports the uninstaller ignores silent mode: it opens a modal and blocks forever while returning success to the caller.

priorFindings.name: simulated operational data labelled live
priorFindings.symptom: After an explicit 'View simulated' action, Metrics showed operational-looking totals (AGENTS LIVE 28 of 91 spawned, TASKS CLOSED 49, TOKEN FLOW 4.9M) on a page carrying a green 'live' label.
priorFindings.machineAStatusClaim: MATERIALLY IMPROVED BUT NOT CLEARED. Measured by lane t5a on the current built renderer: the exact string 'View simulated' is still PRESENT in dist and app.asar (a prior claim of absence was refuted by the harvest verifier's re-measurement); the default metrics state shows em-dash and 'unavailable' on every tile with 'live projection unavailable'; and explicit labels now exist including 'Demonstration data. Nothing in it is running on this computer.' and 'sample board - demonstration traffic, not a live fleet'. NOT ESTABLISHED EITHER WAY: whether any remaining path can still put a green 'live' badge over fabricated numbers. That is B's row to settle.

priorFindings.name: userdata adoption trap
priorFindings.symptom: If %APPDATA%\Mission Control exists from any pre-rename install, the renamed build adopts it, cannot decrypt the adopted agent-spawn-key.enc, and Start is PERMANENTLY DISABLED with nothing on screen explaining why. Clean A/B: with the folder absent a fresh key is created and a session runs.
priorFindings.machineAStatusClaim: OPEN. This is the single most likely cause of a false BLOCKER verdict on B, because B's own machine may carry pre-rename userData from the 2026-08-09 exercise.

priorFindings.name: seeded topology not configurable
priorFindings.symptom: A new user saw a fixed two-machine roster seeded with TEST-NET addresses (192.0.2.x) and Settings offered no configuration for host, endpoint, roster, account, owner identity or machine identity.
priorFindings.machineAStatusClaim: IMPROVED IN THE RENDERER. Measured by lane t5a: the machine selector now reads 'All / Computer 1 / Computer 2' with no IP addresses present. Whether the roster is CONFIGURABLE is not established.

contradictions.matrixSays: After settling and final recheck, no relevant Local/Roaming AppData remains. Retained userData is a defect under the handoff.
contradictions.productDoes: shell/userdata-adoption.cjs deliberately PRESERVES and ADOPTS userData across a product rename, and writes a durable %APPDATA%\ToolsEnabled\.userdata-adoption.json record.
contradictions.why_it_matters: These two cannot both be satisfied by the same build. B will fail 'Removal and leftovers' on retained userData while A has deliberately built retention. This is an owner-level product decision (does uninstall delete a user's data?), not a defect for either machine to fix unilaterally.
contradictions.action: Escalate to the owner before B records a verdict on this row. Do not let either side silently pick a side.

falseVerdictTraps.trap: Pre-rename %APPDATA%\Mission Control present on the test machine
falseVerdictTraps.produces: FALSE BLOCKER - Start permanently disabled, looks like a fresh-install defect
falseVerdictTraps.avoid: Before installing, rename %APPDATA%\Mission Control aside and record that you did. Then run the retained-profile row DELIBERATELY as its own exercise rather than by accident.

falseVerdictTraps.produces: FALSE 'neither present' - which the matrix classes INCONCLUSIVE, not a pass
falseVerdictTraps.avoid: Key names are UNBRACED. Probe both HKCU locations listed in identity.registryGuidCarveOut.probeLocations.

falseVerdictTraps.trap: Quoting a hash taken from a path inside a build output directory
falseVerdictTraps.produces: Certification of a build nobody can reproduce
falseVerdictTraps.avoid: Only hash the frozen copy at candidate.immutableLocation. The build directory reuses one filename per build, so a hash quoted there expires on the next rebuild with no change to the filename.

falseVerdictTraps.trap: Accepting file VersionInfo CompanyName as evidence for the Installed Apps publisher row
falseVerdictTraps.avoid: Read the uninstall registry Publisher value and the Installed Apps UI separately from the file resource. The matrix already says metadata alone is insufficient.

falseVerdictTraps.trap: Taking every 'Recommended' setup answer and concluding the product has no working controls
falseVerdictTraps.produces: Possible FALSE BLOCKER, or a REAL finding - both are valuable but they must not be confused
falseVerdictTraps.avoid: Run first-run TWICE on separate fresh profiles: once accepting every Recommended answer, once choosing the most permissive answer. Report the two click-paths separately. A-side has previously measured that the recommended path granted zero write flags and therefore exposed no control that starts an agent; whether that is still true of the new candidate is unverified.

falseVerdictTraps.trap: Reading a green suite as evidence
falseVerdictTraps.avoid: Machine A's own record is that roughly fifteen defects this sprint all shipped past a green suite and not one was caught by a test. Treat A-side test results as claims to check, never as coverage.
